1 # Python-Markdown: Architecture 2 3 This document describes how the `markdown` package is put together: its main components, three key design decisions (ADRs), and the rules a developer should keep to when changing the code. 4 5 ## 1. Overview 6 7 Python-Markdown turns Markdown text into (X)HTML through a fixed **five-stage pipeline** driven by the `Markdown` class. Each stage is a **priority-ordered registry of processors**. All behaviour, built-in or added, comes from the processors in those registries. **Extensions** change the converter by registering, replacing or removing processors; they never change the pipeline itself. The package has no runtime third-party dependencies (`pyproject.toml` declares none). 8 9 ### Components 10 11 | # | Component | Files | Responsibility | 12 |---|-----------|-------|----------------| 13 | 1 | **Core** | `core.py`, `__init__.py`, `__main__.py` | Public API (`markdown()`, `markdownFromFile()`, `Markdown`, `convert()`, `convertFile()`, the `markdown_py` CLI). `build_parser()` creates the five registries; `registerExtensions()`/`build_extension()` load extensions. Holds shared per-instance state: `htmlStash`, `references`, `ESCAPED_CHARS`, `block_level_elements`, `output_format`/`serializer`. `reset()` clears the per-document state. | 14 | 2 | **Preprocessors** | `preprocessors.py`, `htmlparser.py` | Work on the source as a list of lines before parsing. Defaults: `normalize_whitespace` (30) and `html_block` (20). The latter uses `HTMLExtractor` (`htmlparser.py`) to move raw HTML blocks into the `htmlStash`. | 15 | 3 | **Block parser** | `blockparser.py`, `blockprocessors.py` | `BlockParser.parseDocument()` creates the root element (`md.doc_tag`, a `div`), splits the text into blocks on blank lines, and for each block asks every `BlockProcessor` in priority order whether it applies (`test()`), then calls `run()`. Processors build `ElementTree` elements and may recurse through `parser.parseChunk()`/`parseBlocks()`. A `State` stack (`parser.state`) tracks nesting such as lists. Defaults: `empty` 100, `indent` 90, `code` 80, `hashheader` 70, `setextheader` 60, `hr` 50, `olist` 40, `ulist` 30, `quote` 20, `reference` 15, `paragraph` 10. | 16 | 4 | **Tree processors** | `treeprocessors.py` | Work on the whole `ElementTree` after block parsing. Defaults: `inline` 20 (runs the inline patterns), `prettify` 10 (adds whitespace and newlines), `unescape` 0 (turns backslash-escape placeholders back into characters). | 17 | 5 | **Inline patterns** | `inlinepatterns.py` | Regex-based `InlineProcessor` subclasses whose `handleMatch(m, data)` returns `(element_or_text, start, end)`. The `inline` tree processor applies them to each element's text in priority order. Defaults: `backtick` 190, `escape` 180, `reference` 170, `link` 160, `image_link` 150, `image_reference` 140, `short_reference` 130, `short_image_ref` 125, `autolink` 120, `automail` 110, `linebreak` 100, `html` 90, `entity` 80, `em_strong` 60 (a `DelimiterProcessor` for `*` and `_`). | 18 | 6 | **Serializers and postprocessors** | `serializers.py`, `postprocessors.py` | The serializer (`to_xhtml_string` by default, or `to_html_string`) turns the tree into a string and escapes text and attributes. Postprocessors then work on that string: `raw_html` 30 (replaces stash placeholders with the stored HTML) and `amp_substitute` 20. | 19 | 7 | **Utilities** | `util.py` | Shared building blocks: `Registry`, the `Processor` base class, `AtomicString`, `HtmlStash`, placeholder templates (`STX`/`ETX`-delimited), `BLOCK_LEVEL_ELEMENTS`, and the entry-point lookup `get_installed_extensions()`. | 20 | 8 | **Extensions** | `extensions/__init__.py`, `extensions/*.py` | The `Extension` base class (config handling plus `extendMarkdown(md)`) and 18 built-in extensions (e.g. `tables`, `footnotes`, `def_list`, `fenced_code`, `codehilite`, `admonition`, `smarty`, `meta`). `extra` is a bundle that loads several others. | 21 22 ### How the components call each other 23 24 ```mermaid 25 flowchart LR 26 U["markdown() / Markdown.convert()"] --> C["Core: Markdown"] 27 C -- "__init__: build_parser()" --> R[("Registries (util.Registry)")] 28 C -- "registerExtensions()" --> E["Extensions: extendMarkdown(md)"] 29 E -- "register / deregister" --> R 30 31 subgraph Pipeline["convert(): the five stages"] 32 direction LR 33 P["1. Preprocessors
lines → lines"] --> B["2. BlockParser + BlockProcessors
lines → ElementTree"] 34 B --> T["3. Treeprocessors
tree → tree"] 35 T --> S["4. Serializer
tree → string"] 36 S --> PP["5. Postprocessors
string → string"] 37 T -. "'inline' runs" .-> I["Inline patterns"] 38 end 39 C --> P 40 PP --> O["HTML output"] 41 42 H[("md.htmlStash
md.references")] 43 P -. "store raw HTML" .-> H 44 B -. "store link refs" .-> H 45 I -. "read refs / store HTML" .-> H 46 PP -. "restore raw HTML" .-> H 47 ``` 48 49 Processors reach shared state through the `Markdown` instance. Block processors use `self.parser.md`. Other processors receive it as the optional `md` constructor argument (`self.md`). Built-ins that need no shared state are created without it (e.g. `backtick`, `linebreak`, `amp_substitute`), so a processor that uses `self.md` must be constructed with `md`. Dependencies point one way: `util.py` imports no other module of the package at runtime (only a type-checking import of `Markdown`); the core stage modules depend on `util.py`; extensions depend on the core modules; the core never imports a specific extension. 50 51 ## 2. Architecture Decision Records 52 53 ### ADR-1: A priority-sorted `Registry` for every processing stage 54 55 **Status:** Verified. Commit `6ee07d2` (2018), *"Replace homegrown OrderedDict with purpose-built Registry. (#688)"*, which fixes issue #418. The deprecated compatibility shim was removed in commit `a767b2d` (2022, *"Remove previously deprecated objects"*). Implementation: `markdown/util.py`, class `Registry`. 56 57 **Context.** Processors used to live in a home-grown `OrderedDict` where each item was placed relative to another by a location string (`"_begin"`, `"name"`). Placement depended on which other items happened to be present and on the order extensions were loaded, which made combining extensions fragile. 58 59 **Decision.** Every stage (`preprocessors`, `parser.blockprocessors`, `inlinePatterns`, `treeprocessors`, `postprocessors`) is a `util.Registry`. Items are registered with a **name** and a numeric **priority** and are iterated from highest to lowest priority. Items with equal priority keep their registration order. Registering an existing name replaces the old item, which is then sorted by its new priority. `deregister(name)` removes an item. Items can be looked up by name or index. 60 61 **Alternatives considered.** (a) Keep the relative-location `OrderedDict` API. It was kept only as a deprecated shim and later removed. (b) Use plain lists that extensions insert into by index, which has the same load-order fragility. 62 63 **Consequences.** Placement is independent of load order, and any built-in processor can be replaced or removed by name. On the other hand, priorities act as global "magic numbers": to place a new processor correctly, an author must know the priorities of the built-ins it has to run before or after (listed in §1). 64 65 ### ADR-2: Extensions are found by entry point, with a dotted-path fallback 66 67 **Status:** Verified. Commit `cd73243` (2018), *"Refactor Extension loading (#627)"*. Implementation: `Markdown.build_extension()` in `markdown/core.py` and `util.get_installed_extensions()` in `markdown/util.py`; built-in names are declared in `pyproject.toml`. 68 69 **Context.** Short names such as `'tables'` used to be special-cased to modules inside `markdown.extensions`, and there was also an `mdx_` module-prefix convention. Third-party authors who wanted short names told users to copy files into the package. 70 71 **Decision.** A string name passed in `extensions=[...]` is first looked up in the `markdown.extensions` **entry-point group** of the installed distributions. If no entry point matches, the string is treated as a dotted import path `package.module[:ClassName]`. Without a class name, the module's `makeExtension(**kwargs)` is called. Extension *instances* may also be passed directly. All built-ins are declared under `[project.entry-points.'markdown.extensions']` in `pyproject.toml`. 72 73 **Alternatives considered.** (a) Keep special-casing the `markdown.extensions` package and the `mdx_` prefix (removed in this change). (b) Require full dotted paths for everything, which would break existing short names. 74 75 **Consequences.** Third-party extensions get short names on the same terms as built-ins, and dotted paths still work without packaging. On the other hand, a short name exists only in **installed** package metadata: a new or renamed entry point takes effect only after the distribution is (re)installed, and until then the string is treated as a module path. 76 77 ### ADR-3: `ElementTree` as the document model; raw HTML and protected text kept out of reach 78 79 **Status:** Inferred. The switch is recorded (commit `a218ebb`, 2008, *"ElementTree support added"*, which replaced the earlier home-grown `NanoDom`), `serializers.py` says it was *"taken from ElementTree 1.3 preview"*, and the `HtmlStash` docstring describes the stash. No commit or issue states the *reasons*, so the rationale below is our own reading of the code. 80 81 **Context.** A Markdown document mixes structure (paragraphs, lists, emphasis) with raw HTML that must pass through untouched. A pipeline of string substitutions (the original `Markdown.pl` approach) gives later steps no view of the structure and can easily process the same text twice. 82 83 **Decision.** Block parsing builds an `xml.etree.ElementTree`. Later stages work on elements, and the package's own serializers produce HTML or XHTML. Content that must not be treated as Markdown is kept out of reach in two ways. (1) **Raw HTML** is not put into the tree: it is stored in `md.htmlStash` and replaced by a placeholder (`STX + "wzxhzdk:N" + ETX`), which the `raw_html` postprocessor swaps back after serialization. (2) **Text that must not be processed by further inline patterns** is wrapped in `util.AtomicString`, which the `inline` tree processor skips. Backslash escapes follow the same idea: the `escape` pattern replaces an escaped character with an `STX`/`ETX` placeholder, and the `unescape` tree processor restores it at the end. 84 85 **Alternatives considered.** (a) A string-only pipeline. (b) The earlier custom DOM (`NanoDom`). (c) Parsing raw HTML into the tree, which would need a full HTML parser and would normalise or re-escape the user's HTML. 86 87 **Consequences.** Extensions can inspect and rewrite structure with tree processors, and output escaping happens in one place, the serializer. On the other hand, content travels on two channels, the tree and the stash, and developers must use the right one. Text placed in an element is escaped on output, so markup must be stored in the stash or built as elements. Placeholders also appear as ordinary text inside the tree, so tree processors see placeholders rather than the HTML behind them. 88 89 ## 3. Constraints 90 91 | # | Rule | Where it is visible | 92 |---|------|---------------------| 93 | C1 | **Change the pipeline only through the Registry API.** Add, replace or remove processors with `register(item, name, priority)` / `deregister(name)` on the instance's registries (`md.preprocessors`, `md.parser.blockprocessors`, `md.inlinePatterns`, `md.treeprocessors`, `md.postprocessors`). Do not edit the default `build_*` functions to add optional behaviour, and choose priorities relative to the built-ins. | `markdown/util.py` (`Registry`); `markdown/core.py` (`build_parser`); defaults in the `build_*` functions of each stage module | 94 | C2 | **Extensions follow the extension contract.** Subclass `markdown.extensions.Extension`, declare options as `self.config = {name: [default, description]}` before calling `super().__init__(**kwargs)`, read them with `getConfig`/`getConfigs`, do all wiring in `extendMarkdown(md)`, and provide a module-level `makeExtension(**kwargs)`. Built-ins live in `markdown/extensions/` and are listed as entry points in `pyproject.toml`. | `markdown/extensions/__init__.py`; `pyproject.toml` (`[project.entry-points.'markdown.extensions']`); any built-in such as `markdown/extensions/admonition.py` | 95 | C3 | **Dependencies point one way.** Core modules (`core.py`, `blockparser.py`, `blockprocessors.py`, `inlinepatterns.py`, `treeprocessors.py`, `preprocessors.py`, `postprocessors.py`, `serializers.py`, `util.py`) must not import any specific extension module. The only extension imports in the core are of the `Extension` base class (in `core.py` and the package `__init__.py`). Extensions may import core modules. | Import blocks of `markdown/core.py` and `markdown/__init__.py`; imports of the other core modules | 96 | C4 | **Use the right channel for protected content.** Raw HTML that must reach the output unchanged goes through `md.htmlStash.store()`. Text that later inline patterns must not touch is an `util.AtomicString`. Never put pre-rendered HTML into element text or attributes: the serializer will escape it. | `markdown/util.py` (`AtomicString`, `HtmlStash`); `markdown/treeprocessors.py` (`InlineProcessor` skips `AtomicString`); `markdown/postprocessors.py` (`RawHtmlPostprocessor`) | 97 | C5 | **Per-document state must be resettable.** One `Markdown` instance may convert many documents. State that belongs to one document lives on the instance (e.g. `htmlStash`, `references`) or on an extension. An extension with such state calls `md.registerExtension(self)` and implements `reset()`, which `Markdown.reset()` calls. | `markdown/core.py` (`registerExtension`, `reset`) | 98

39	def slugify(value: str, separator: str, unicode: bool = False) -> str:
40	    """ Slugify a string, to make it URL friendly. """
41	    if not unicode:
42	        # Replace Extended Latin characters with ASCII, i.e. `žlutý` => `zluty`
43	        value = unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', value)
44	        value = value.encode('ascii', 'ignore').decode('ascii')
45	    value = re.sub(r'[^\w\s-]', '', value).strip().lower()
46	    return re.sub(r'[{}\s]+'.format(separator), separator, value)
47	
48	
49	def slugify_unicode(value: str, separator: str) -> str:
50	    """ Slugify a string, to make it URL friendly while preserving Unicode characters. """
51	    return slugify(value, separator, unicode=True)
52

# Table of Contents Extension for Python-Markdown
# ===============================================

# See https://Python-Markdown.github.io/extensions/toc
# for documentation.

# Original code Copyright 2008 [Jack Miller](https://codezen.org/)

# All changes Copyright 2008-2024 The Python Markdown Project

# License: [BSD](https://opensource.org/licenses/bsd-license.php)

"""
Add table of contents support to Python-Markdown.

See the [documentation](https://Python-Markdown.github.io/extensions/toc)
for details.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from . import Extension
from ..treeprocessors import Treeprocessor
from ..util import parseBoolValue, AMP_SUBSTITUTE, deprecated, HTML_PLACEHOLDER_RE, AtomicString
from ..treeprocessors import UnescapeTreeprocessor
from ..serializers import RE_AMP
from ..inlinepatterns import HTML_RE
import re
import html
import unicodedata
from copy import deepcopy
import xml.etree.ElementTree as etree
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Iterator, MutableSet

if TYPE_CHECKING:  # pragma: no cover
    from markdown import Markdown


def slugify(value: str, separator: str, unicode: bool = False) -> str:
    """ Slugify a string, to make it URL friendly. """
    if not unicode:
        # Replace Extended Latin characters with ASCII, i.e. `žlutý` => `zluty`
        value = unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', value)
        value = value.encode('ascii', 'ignore').decode('ascii')
    value = re.sub(r'[^\w\s-]', '', value).strip().lower()
    return re.sub(r'[{}\s]+'.format(separator), separator, value)


def slugify_unicode(value: str, separator: str) -> str:
    """ Slugify a string, to make it URL friendly while preserving Unicode characters. """
    return slugify(value, separator, unicode=True)


IDCOUNT_RE = re.compile(r'^(.*)_([0-9]+)$')


def unique(id: str, ids: MutableSet[str], counters: dict[str, int] | None = None) -> str:
    """ Ensure id is unique in set of ids. Append '_1', '_2'... if not

    `counters` is an optional cache which maps a base id to the highest `n` for which
    `base_1` through `base_n` are all known to be in `ids`. When the same cache is passed
    along with the same `ids` on every call, a repeated id skips past the suffixes which
    earlier calls already found to be taken rather than checking each of them again.
    """
    if id in ids or not id:
        m = IDCOUNT_RE.match(id)
        if m:
            base, count = m.group(1), int(m.group(2))
        else:
            base, count = id, 0
        skip = False
        if counters is not None:
            known = counters.get(base, 0)
            # Only skip ahead when this id falls within the run of suffixes known to be
            # taken, or is the next one after it, as any later suffix may still be free.
            if count <= known or id == f'{base}_{known + 1}':
                skip = True
                count = max(count, known)
        count += 1
        while f'{base}_{count}' in ids:
            count += 1
        id = f'{base}_{count}'
        if skip:
            # Every suffix from `base_1` through the new id is now known to be taken.
            counters[base] = count
    ids.add(id)
    return id


@deprecated('Use `render_inner_html` and `striptags` instead.')
def get_name(el: etree.Element) -> str:
    """Get title name."""

    text = []
    for c in el.itertext():
        if isinstance(c, AtomicString):
            text.append(html.unescape(c))
        else:
            text.append(c)
    return ''.join(text).strip()


@deprecated('Use `run_postprocessors`, `render_inner_html` and/or `striptags` instead.')
def stashedHTML2text(text: str, md: Markdown, strip_entities: bool = True) -> str:
    """ Extract raw HTML from stash, reduce to plain text and swap with placeholder. """
    def _html_sub(m: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        """ Substitute raw html with plain text. """
        try:
            raw = md.htmlStash.rawHtmlBlocks[int(m.group(1))]
        except (IndexError, TypeError):  # pragma: no cover
            return m.group(0)
        # Strip out tags and/or entities - leaving text
        res = re.sub(r'(<[^>]+>)', '', raw)
        if strip_entities:
            res = re.sub(r'(&[\#a-zA-Z0-9]+;)', '', res)
        return res

    return HTML_PLACEHOLDER_RE.sub(_html_sub, text)

# Design: Readable default TOC anchors for non-Latin headings

## Approach

Make two small changes to the module-level `slugify` helper in `markdown/extensions/toc.py`. The extension wiring, the registry and `unique()` stay as they are.

1. **Fallback (FR-001).** In ASCII mode (`unicode=False`), compute the ASCII slug as today. If that slug is empty, return `slugify(original_value, separator, unicode=True)`. The fallback must use the **original** `value`, not the NFKD-decomposed one. Otherwise Cyrillic letters such as `й` would come out as a base letter plus a separate combining mark, because FR-002 now keeps marks. Headings that already have a non-empty ASCII slug take the same code path as before. This covers Latin, extended-Latin and mixed headings such as `Setup Настройка` → `setup`. A heading with no word characters in any script still returns `''`, so `unique()` still gives it `_1`.
2. **Keep combining marks (FR-002).** Python's `re` has no `\p{M}`, and `[^\w\s-]` drops Mn/Mc characters such as Devanagari vowel signs and the virama. Replace the single `re.sub(r'[^\w\s-]', '', value)` with a filter that keeps a character if it matches `[\w\s-]` **or** if `unicodedata.category(c)` is `Mn` or `Mc`. In ASCII mode this changes nothing, because the ASCII encode step has already removed every combining mark. So only Unicode slugs are affected (`slugify_unicode` and the new fallback). Punctuation is still stripped (`ヘッダー!` → `ヘッダー`).

**Why this fits the architecture:** the change stays inside the `toc` extension, which follows the extension contract (C2). The `slugify` config option keeps its current default object (`slugify`), so users who pass their own callable get exactly what they got before (AC-FR-001-07). No core module changes, so the one-way dependency rule (C3) holds. Only the standard library (`re`, `unicodedata`) is used, so the package still has no runtime dependencies (§1 Overview). No processor, priority or per-document state changes, so ADR-1 and C1/C5 are not affected.

**Main alternative rejected:** a new function (e.g. `slugify_fallback`) as the new default value of the `slugify` config option. I rejected it for two reasons:
- Users and tools that pass `slugify=markdown.extensions.toc.slugify` explicitly would still get `_N` ids.
- It adds public API for no benefit.

I also rejected making `slugify_unicode` the default (spec Q-001 option B), because it would change ids for every accented Latin heading.

## Change plan

| File | Symbol | Change |
|------|--------|--------|
| `markdown/extensions/toc.py` | `slugify` | modify: keep the original `value`. In ASCII mode, if the ASCII slug is empty, return the Unicode slug of the original value. Replace `re.sub(r'[^\w\s-]', '', value)` with a per-character filter that also keeps characters whose `unicodedata.category` is `Mn` or `Mc`. Then `.strip().lower()` and collapse separators/whitespace as today. Update the docstring to describe the fallback. |
| `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_toc.py` | `TestTOC` | add: tests for AC-FR-001-01 to -07 and AC-FR-002-01 to -03, as `assertMarkdownRenders` with default `toc`, `TocExtension(slugify=slugify_unicode)` and `TocExtension(slugify=lambda value, separator: 'custom')`. Also add a direct unit test that `slugify('Žlutý kůň', '-') == 'zluty-kun'` (AC-FR-002-04). |
| `docs/changelog.md` | - | modify: add an entry under the unreleased section saying that the default `slugify` now falls back to a Unicode slug when the ASCII slug would be empty, and that Unicode slugs keep combining marks. |
| `docs/extensions/toc.md` | - | modify: in the `slugify` option description, explain the non-Latin fallback of the default function (optional, not covered by an AC). |

## Acceptance criteria coverage

| AC | Satisfied by |
|----|--------------|
| AC-FR-001-01 | Fallback in `slugify`: `Введение` → ASCII slug is empty → Unicode slug `введение`. |
| AC-FR-001-02 | Fallback plus the existing separator collapse in `slugify` → `быстрый-старт`. The TOC href is built from the same id in `TocTreeprocessor.run`. |
| AC-FR-001-03 | Fallback gives `введение` both times. The existing `unique()` adds `_1` to the second one. |
| AC-FR-001-04 | ASCII path unchanged in `slugify` (slug not empty, so no fallback): `zluty-kun`, `hello-world`. |
| AC-FR-001-05 | ASCII slug `setup` is not empty, so no fallback. |
| AC-FR-001-06 | `!!!` → the ASCII and Unicode slugs are both empty → `''` → existing `unique()` → `_1`. |
| AC-FR-001-07 | No change to the `TocExtension` config or `TocTreeprocessor`. A user callable is still used as-is. |
| AC-FR-002-01 | Fallback (default config) plus the Mn/Mc-preserving filter in `slugify` → `परिचय`. |
| AC-FR-002-02 | Mn/Mc-preserving filter on the Unicode path (`slugify_unicode` → `slugify(..., unicode=True)`) → `नमस्ते-दुनिया`. |
| AC-FR-002-03 | The filter still drops characters that are neither `\w`, whitespace, `-` nor Mn/Mc, so `!` is removed → `unicode-ヘッダー`. |
| AC-FR-002-04 | ASCII path of `slugify` unchanged (NFKD plus ASCII encode, and no marks are left to keep) → `zluty-kun`. |

## Risks

- **Changed default ids for non-Latin headings.** Headings that used to get `_N` now get readable ids. Any external links to `#_1` and similar on such pages will break. This is accepted by ASSUMP-001 / Q-001 option A, and should go in the changelog. No existing test expects `_N` ids: a search of `tests/` for `id="_N"` and `#_N` found nothing.
- **ASCII-mode output must not change.** The existing default-slug tests in `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_toc.py` (`TestTOC`) guard this, along with the new AC-FR-001-04, -05 and AC-FR-002-04.
- **Unicode-mode output for existing users.** `slugify_unicode` users whose headings contain combining marks (Indic scripts, or decomposed Latin input) will see marks kept where they used to be dropped. This is the intended FR-002 fix. `TestTOC.testPermalinkWithUnicodeInID` and `testPermalinkWithUnicodeTitle` protect the Japanese case, which has no Mn/Mc characters in NFC. Text in NFD form will now keep its marks in Unicode slugs. That matches the changelog note "Make the `slugify_unicode` function not remove diacritical marks (#1118)".
- **Fallback must use the un-normalised value.** If the implementation used the NFKD string, slugs for Cyrillic `й`/`ё` would contain decomposed sequences that do not match what users type. A test with such a heading (e.g. `# Настройка`, or one containing `й`) during implementation would catch this. The AC tests above do not cover it directly.
- **Third parties importing `markdown.extensions.toc.slugify`** (e.g. site generators) will also get the fallback. The output differs only where it used to be an empty string.
- **Security:** the issue text contains no instructions aimed at the agent, so I found no prompt-injection risk.

Punctuation is still stripped (`ヘッダー!` → `ヘッダー`).

**Why this fits the architecture:** the change stays inside the `toc` extension, which follows the extension contract (C2). The `slugify` config option keeps its current default object (`slugify`), so users who pass their own callable get exactly what they got before (AC-FR-001-07). No core module changes, so the one-way dependency rule (C3) holds. Only the standard library (`re`, `unicodedata`) is used, so the package still has no runtime dependencies (§1 Overview). No processor, priority or per-document state changes, so ADR-1 and C1/C5 are not affected.

**Main alternative rejected:** a new function (e.g. `slugify_fallback`) as the new default value of the `slugify` config option. I rejected it for two reasons:
- Users and tools that pass `slugify=markdown.extensions.toc.slugify` explicitly would still get `_N` ids.
- It adds public API for no benefit.

I also rejected making `slugify_unicode` the default (spec Q-001 option B), because it would change ids for every accented Latin heading.

## Risks

- **Changed default ids for non-Latin headings.** Headings that used to get `_N` now get readable ids. Any external links to `#_1` and similar on such pages will break. This is accepted by ASSUMP-001 / Q-001 option A, and should go in the changelog. No existing test expects `_N` ids: a search of `tests/` for `id="_N"` and `#_N` found nothing.
- **ASCII-mode output must not change.** The existing default-slug tests in `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_toc.py` (`TestTOC`) guard this, along with the new AC-FR-001-04, -05 and AC-FR-002-04.
- **Unicode-mode output for existing users.** `slugify_unicode` users whose headings contain combining marks (Indic scripts, or decomposed Latin input) will see marks kept where they used to be dropped. This is the intended FR-002 fix. `TestTOC.testPermalinkWithUnicodeInID` and `testPermalinkWithUnicodeTitle` protect the Japanese case, which has no Mn/Mc characters in NFC. Text in NFD form will now keep its marks in Unicode slugs. That matches the changelog note "Make the `slugify_unicode` function not remove diacritical marks (#1118)".
- **Fallback must use the un-normalised value.** If the implementation used the NFKD string, slugs for Cyrillic `й`/`ё` would contain decomposed sequences that do not match what users type. A test with such a heading (e.g. `# Настройка`, or one containing `й`) during implementation would catch this. The AC tests above do not cover it directly.
- **Third parties importing `markdown.extensions.toc.slugify`** (e.g. site generators) will also get the fallback. The output differs only where it used to be an empty string.
- **Security:** the issue text contains no instructions aimed at the agent, so I found no prompt-injection risk.
